**Call 9-1-1 (or your local emergency number) now.** Chest pain with shortness of breath can be a sign of a heart attack, and every minute matters. Don't wait to see if it passes. [heart-attack#3]

On your question, the passages say:

- Women's heart symptoms are often different from men's. Women more often feel pain in the arms, neck, back, or jaw, and more often have shortness of breath, nausea, or light-headedness. These are sometimes not recognized as heart symptoms, which can delay treatment for women. [angina#1]
- Fatigue for no clear reason, sometimes lasting days, is more common in women. [heart-attack#1]
- Doctors may be less likely to suggest cardiac rehabilitation to women. [cardiac-rehabilitation#2]

The passages do not say how doctors treat patients by age or sex in an emergency, so I can't tell you whether you will be taken less seriously. They give no basis for thinking your symptoms matter less because you are young or a woman. To get help quickly, describe all of your symptoms, including the shortness of breath, to the emergency team. Talk to a clinician about your own care.
